posts.cooked:
OK...  that was unexpected...  I just unlocked him!

 

I didn't use The Scholar's whole deck.  I didn't discard a ton of cards.  I didn't immediately defeat Gloomy after The Scholar got incapped.  In fact, The Scholar got incapped quite early and I thought there was no way I'd unlock him, but I might as well try continuing!

 

I'm not sure what the difference is to my previous attempts...  but here's all the info I can gather from the log for further help to others.  I'll list everything that happened to a Scholar card, just in case it helps.  I'll provide a summary of what I think might be the key at the end.

 

The Scholar, Haka and Ra battling Gloomweaver in Insula Primalis.

 

Turn 1:

The Scholar plays Don't Dismiss Anything.
Don't Dismiss Anything puts Know When to Hold Fast into play.

Turn 2:

The Scholar plays Bring What You Need.
The Scholar uses the power on Bring What You Need.

Turn 3:

The Scholar plays Keep Moving.
Keep Moving puts Solid to Liquid into play.
Keep Moving plays Mortal Form to Energy.
The Scholar uses the power on The Scholar.

Turn 4:

The Scholar discards Grace Under Fire.
The Scholar discards Flesh to Iron.
The Scholar plays "Get Out of the Way!".
The Scholar uses the power on Bring What You Need.

Turn 5:

Solid to Liquid destroys itself!
Mortal Form to Energy destroys itself!
The Scholar plays Offensive Transmutation.
The Scholar uses the power on Bring What You Need.
Primordial Plant Life destroys Bring What You Need!

Turn 6:

The Scholar plays Alchemical Redirection.
The Scholar uses the power on The Scholar.
The Scholar takes 20 damage (mostly redirected, as River of Lava and Cursed Acolyte both came out)

Turn 7:

Alchemical Redirection destroys itself!
The Scholar plays Keep Moving.
Keep Moving puts Mortal Form to Energy into play.
Keep Moving plays Solid to Liquid.
The Scholar uses the power on The Scholar.
River of Lava moved Keep Moving from The Scholar's deck to The Scholar's trash.
River of Lava moved Offensive Transmutation from The Scholar's deck to The Scholar's trash.
River of Lava moved Know When to Turn Loose from The Scholar's deck to The Scholar's trash.
A pair of Cursed Acolytes come out together and incapacitate The Scholar

Turn 8:

The Scholar uses the incapacitated ability "One hero may use a power now."

Turns 9-15:

The Scholar uses the incapacitated ability "Up to 2 hero targets regain 1 HP each."
 

I know I have played this combination of cards before, so I don't think any of them was important.  I know I have discarded a ton more cards before, so that can't be it.  The only other villain I've fought in the meantime from the previous attempts was Miss Information, who I had already defeated once before.  The Scholar was on that team, so perhas there's a condition that The Scholar defeats Miss Information, then The Scholar defeats Gloomweaver, but I really doubt that.

What I do think it might be is the amount of healing I did to others.  In all my other attempts, I never healed the other heroes much at all.  I would us Proverbs and Axioms at most once per run.  Perhaps that's the key.

 

 

So my current guess to the unlock condition is:

Defeat Gloomweaver with The Scholar on the team while The Scholar is incapacitated.  During the fight, The Scholar must heal other heroes for a total of X HP or more.

 

I think X may be around 10, but I'm not sure.  Or perhaps X is 20 and the heroes include The Scholar, but I'm fairly sure I've healed that much before too.

 

If anyone else can test out my healing others idea, that'd be great.

Upon reflection I really suspect the healing is incidental. Scanning other unlocks it seems mortal form to energy was a required elemental card. That card is unique because it takes healing and turns it into damage. It sort of fits the idea of him being a gateway. Healing in one place becomes damage in another and he is the conduit. Rather than heal you probably need to heal and turn it into a minimum amount of energy damage accross the game. If you are sandbagging scholar it is still pretty easy for him to throw out some good damage numbers as he starts to fall. You have to be actively playing him poorly to have him not contribute to taking out a relic and zombies. I played two games where I was just playing him attrociously and I didn't get the unlock. Someone needs to do the experiment. Heal him for a lot but never put mortal to energy form out. I predict no unlock if heal without chaining it to damage.

It seems like he doesn't want to tell anyone else about it but somehow it seems the Scholar discovered the aweful truth that he is a character in a comic book themed cooperative deck game. He stops with the healing and starts destroying his deck for damage. His new version turns card discard into damage so it is more set up to use the iron cards and build up your deck for a big haka style finish (now you will get 2x your hand size in damage which is much more appealing for a KO). Because of the damage angle of new power I suspect the unlock might be more about damage than just healing.

posts.name: SandyStriker
posts.cooked:
If you want the unlock you can avoid the iron form it doesn't help you much and it has been shown to not be needed.

If you want to help the community, play a game without using the energy form but with a high amount of healing, probably that will not be an unlock but I'd like to know whether it is healing a minimum amount or a minimum amount of zapping that unlocks the infinite.

If you just want to go straight to the unlock do a lot of heal zapping, that has yet to fail and is easy to do. The problem is nobody has tried healing a lot while restraining from zapping. (along with beating gloomweaver with scholar down of course)

posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked:
Just got him.  I did use Solid to Liquid and do a decent amount of healing, and I used Flesh to Iron, but pretty sure that MFtE never came out.  However, I did use Alchemical Redirection, but it did NOT kill him (Unload did that).  I defeated Gloomweaver as part of the same Unload action that downed Gloomweaver.

 

My theory:

Defeat Gloomweaver after Scholar is incapacitated, Alchemical Redirection must have been played.

 

Possibly adding in some minimum amount of healing or 1 form being played.

 

Edit: In all of my previous, failed unlocks, I got multiple forms and TONS of heal zapping (and thus healing), but I feel like Alchemical Redirection was the missing piece.

posts.name: SandyStriker
posts.cooked:
Certainly if you are trying to have scholar go down Alchemical Redirection will be a good card to play. I wonder if anyone recalls unlocking without having played Alchemical Redirection. One of the earliest succesful unlocks suggested Alchemical Redirection was perhaps not neccesary but the poster wasn't sure. After that it seems like most unlocks do use it at some point, it is an obvious choice if you want him incapped.

I did play the redirection as a part of a game to incap him quick and clean and was surprised to not get the unlock. I avoided healing him because what was the point if he was supposed to get incapped? Thus I guess there is some minimum amount of healing but it probably isn't anything too impressive.

Some unlocks appear to have only moderate scholar healing and considering he has an innate power and a good portion of his deck heals, it is probably pretty easy to hit the mark unless you are actively avoiding the healing.

posts.name: jorgenp
posts.cooked: My attempts definitely seemed to indicate healing was necessary.  All my failed attempts trying to play out his deck, even shuffling it, never involved healing to any large degree, as I too thought what was the point of healing if the goal is to incap him.  The only real difference in my successful unlock to previous ones was that I used his incapped healing ability a lot, because The Scholar went down a lot earlier than I expected him to and the other heroes were in trouble.
